title: Search Your Feelings
author: Andrew Ellison
summary: Andrew Ellison uses a viral TikTok video of high school students struggling to read aloud and explain a simple sentence as a lens for examining the legacy of Ken Goodman's Three Cues method in American education. Goodman's approach, pioneered in a 1967 paper, deprioritized phonics in favor of context and 'sense-making,' effectively teaching children that a word approximating the context is good enough. Ellison traces how this produced generations of students who guess rather than decode -- and how Goodman's own stated indifference to word-level accuracy ('the purpose is to make sense') reveals a philosophical incoherence that has persisted in school districts for decades. The essay blends sharp humor with serious analysis, connecting the TikTok video directly to root causes in reading science denialism. Ellison is a senior writer for Cana Academy and VP of Enrollment Management at the University of Dallas.
points: * A viral TikTok video shows high school students at a science/technology charter school unable to correctly read aloud or explain simple sentences -- evidence of deep, systemic instructional failure. * Ken Goodman's Three Cues method (1967) taught children to use context, picture cues, and syntax to guess words rather than decode through phonics -- effectively saying approximate matches are acceptable. * Students trained via Three Cues reconstruct meaning instead of reading text; one student in the video substitutes an entire interpretation that 'makes sense' while missing the actual words. * Goodman in a 2019 interview: 'The purpose is not to learn words. The purpose is to make sense.' He also claimed a horse and pony are 'the same concept.' * Three Cues has been scientifically debunked for decades, yet its shadow looms long -- the methods persist because they were adopted system-wide and are ideologically resistant to revision. * Effective remediation requires rigorous repetitive training: 'do it on the spot and unexpectedly in the middle of class... Just keep doing it over and over, and do not for one second balk because you are afraid of making struggling students feel uncomfortable.'
quotes: These kids in the TikTok video aren't the victims of COVID and school closures, or brain-dead illiterate social media addicts... they are Ken Goodman's kids.
THINK OF SOME WORD THAT STARTS WITH THE SAME FIRST LETTER THAT YOU SEE HERE. IT'S PROBABLY CLOSE ENOUGH.
'The purpose is not to learn words,' he said. 'The purpose is to make sense.'
'Word recognition is a preoccupation. I don't teach word recognition. I teach people to make sense of language. And learning the words is incidental to that.'

Training means rigor and repetition -- do it on the spot and unexpectedly in the middle of class... Just keep doing it over and over, and do not for one second balk because you are afraid of making struggling students feel uncomfortable.
It would be a better world if more teachers of all subjects at all grade levels acted more like ursine Romanian Olympic gymnastics coaches and less like volunteer pre-K church childcare staff.
